cases.input: Tests for new parser behavior assert only that an internal mock is called once, without asserting return values, errors, or caller-visible state.
cases.expected: The testing reviewer reports a false-confidence gap and requests state/behavior outcome proof.
forbidden: Treat mock call count as complete behavior verification
Assume coverage is sufficient merely because tests exist

cases.input: An integration test fake bypasses serialization, permission middleware, and error translation while claiming to cover the real client-to-service path.
cases.expected: The testing reviewer reports a double fidelity gap and requests the narrowest real-object or high-fidelity integration proof.
forbidden: Treat a fake that bypasses critical boundaries as integration proof
Only add more of the same mock interactions

cases.input: The public protocol explicitly requires exactly one audit sink call on failure; the test asserts that call and its arguments.
cases.expected: Keep suppression; a call-count assertion is appropriate proof when the interaction itself is the contract.
forbidden: Report a public protocol interaction as brittle implementation coupling
Require a state assertion that cannot observe the sink

cases.input: The diff adds production code and passing tests, but the reviewer has no worker execution RED or characterization evidence.
cases.expected: Do not infer that the developer skipped TDD; assess only current assertion proof and leave execution history ownership to spec-work.
forbidden: Report missing TDD from the final diff
Promote green tests into RED-history evidence
